definitions.explanation: The transition from wakefulness to sleep. Often used in medical or health-related contexts.

examples.japanese: {入眠|にゅうみん}に{時間|じかん}がかかる。
examples.english: It takes time to fall asleep.

examples.japanese: スマホを{見|み}ると{入眠|にゅうみん}が{遅|おく}れやすい。
examples.english: Looking at your phone tends to delay sleep onset.

examples.japanese: {寝|ね}る{前|まえ}にリラックスする{習慣|しゅうかん}をつけると、スムーズに{入眠|にゅうみん}できるようになる。
examples.english: If you make a habit of relaxing before bed, you'll be able to fall asleep more smoothly.

notes:
Composed of {入|にゅう} (entering) + {眠|みん} (sleep). A somewhat formal or technical term commonly used in health articles, sleep research, and medical contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {入眠|にゅうみん}{障害|しょうがい} (difficulty falling asleep, a type of insomnia)
- {入眠|にゅうみん}{儀式|ぎしき} (bedtime ritual)
- スムーズな{入眠|にゅうみん} (smooth sleep onset)
- {入眠|にゅうみん}までの{時間|じかん} (time to fall asleep)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {寝|ね}つき — falling asleep (more colloquial; {寝|ね}つきが{良|よ}い/{悪|わる}い is the common way to describe ease of falling asleep)
- {就寝|しゅうしん} — going to bed, retiring for the night (focuses on the act of going to bed, not the physiological transition)
- {睡眠|すいみん} — sleep (the state itself, not the process of falling asleep)
